f: Step 1: Nyquist needs fs at least 7620 Hz, so 3820 Hz undersamples. Step 2: alias = |3810 - 1 x 3820| = 10 Hz. Check: 10 lies in [0, 1910], the representable baseband.

q: Bandwidth B = 266 kHz and SNR = 55 dB. The Shannon capacity is approximately (bps): (spaced-repetition variant 11304)
h: C = B log2(1 + SNR), with SNR converted from dB first.
f: Step 1: SNR linear = 10^(55/10) = 316227.766. Step 2: C = 266000 x log2(1 + 316227.766) which is about 4859982 bps. Check: Shannon is an upper bound; a practical rate must stay below it, then Nyquist sets the levels.

q: AM with modulating bandwidth BWm = 296 kHz has total transmission bandwidth:
h: AM keeps both sidebands: BWt = 2 x BWm.
f: Step 1: sidebands sit at fc +/- up to 296 kHz. Step 2: BWt = 2 x 296 = 592 kHz. Check: SSB would need only 296 kHz, at the cost of sharper filtering.

q: A state matrix A has characteristic polynomial lambda^2 + (245) lambda + (12556). Its eigenvalues (the system poles) are: (spaced-repetition variant 11304)
h: Factor the quadratic: (lambda - r1)(lambda - r2).
f: Step 1: lambda^2 + (245) lambda + (12556) = (lambda - (-73))(lambda - (-172)). Step 2: eigenvalues are -73 and -172. Check: sum of roots = -245, product = 12556, matching trace and determinant relations.

q: Total energy of x(t) = e^(-808 t) u(t) (1 ohm reference) is: (spaced-repetition variant 11305)
h: E = integral of e^(-2a t) from 0 to infinity.
f: Step 1: square the signal: |x|^2 = e^(-1616 t) for t at least 0. Step 2: E = 1/(2a) with a = 808, so E = 0.0006. Check: finite positive energy, so this is an energy signal with P = 0.

q: For y(t) = x(17 t - 1258), the time shift (after factoring) is:
h: Rewrite as x(a (t - b/a)) and read off the shift.
f: Step 1: 17 t - 1258 = 17 (t - 74). Step 2: compression by 17 with shift right by 74. Check: the common wrong answer is 1258, the unfactored constant.

q: The system y(t) = 141 x(t) + 338 is:
o: Linear: it is a straight-line graph
Time-varying but linear
Memoryless, therefore linear
Nonlinear: zero input gives output 338, violating the zero-in zero-out rule
h: Test x = 0 first; a linear system must answer 0.
f: Step 1: with x(t) = 0 the output is 338, not 0. Step 2: superposition fails, so the system is nonlinear (affine). Check: the term 141 x(t) alone would be linear; the offset 338 breaks it.

q: For x[n] = {470, 252} and h[n] = {327, 891}, the sum of all output samples (sum of y[n]) is:
h: Sum of a convolution = (sum of x) x (sum of h).
f: Step 1: sum of x = 722, sum of h = 1218. Step 2: product = 879396. Check: direct convolution gives y = {153690, 501174, 224532}, summing to 879396.

q: H(s) has denominator s^2 + (40) s + (0), i.e. poles at s = 0 and s = -40. For the causal system: (spaced-repetition variant 11305)
o: Unstable only if the zeros are in the right-half plane
Anticausal and stable for every ROC
Causal but unstable: a pole is not in the left-half plane
Stable because the poles are real
h: Causal + stable needs every pole strictly in the left-half plane.
f: Step 1: poles are 0 and -40. Step 2: at least one pole is not negative, so the causal ROC excludes part or all of the jw axis: not BIBO stable. Check: zeros do not decide stability.

q: A causal discrete-time LTI system has a single pole at z = 0.815. It is: (spaced-repetition variant 11305)
o: Unstable only for complex poles
Causal and stable: pole inside the unit circle
Stable whenever the pole is real
Stable because the ROC is outside the pole
h: Causal + stable needs every pole strictly inside |z| = 1.
f: Step 1: |pole| = 0.815 is below 1. Step 2: the causal ROC outside the pole therefore includes the unit circle: stable.

q: A filter has peak magnitude response 178. At its 3-dB frequency the magnitude is: (spaced-repetition variant 11305)
h: 3-dB means half power, so magnitude scales by 1/sqrt(2).
f: Step 1: |H| at 3-dB = 178 / sqrt(2). Step 2: = 125.865. Check: (125.865)^2 is approximately half of 178^2 = 31684, confirming half power.

q: A signal band-limited to fm = 400.7 kHz has Nyquist rate:
h: Nyquist rate = 2 fm.
f: Step 1: rate = 2 x 400.7 kHz. Step 2: = 801.4 kHz minimum sampling rate. Check: sampling exactly at this rate is phase-sensitive, so real systems add margin and an anti-alias filter.

q: A noiseless B = 1168 kHz channel must carry 28032 kbps by the Nyquist formula. The number of signal levels L needed is:
h: Rate = 2B log2(L); solve for L.
f: Step 1: log2(L) = 28032 / (2 x 1168) = 12. Step 2: L = 2^12 = 4096. Check: L is a power of two, as a whole number of bits per symbol requires.

q: An AM carrier has Pc = 568 W and modulation index mu = 0.22. Total transmitted power is:
h: Ptot = Pc (1 + mu^2 / 2).
f: Step 1: mu^2/2 = 0.0242. Step 2: Ptot = 568 x 1.0242 = 581.75 W. Check: sideband efficiency rises with mu and peaks at 33 percent when mu = 1, motivating DSB-SC and SSB.

q: A continuous-time state model has dominant eigenvalue lambda = -506 (real). The free response is: (spaced-repetition variant 11305)
o: Stable: dominant eigenvalue has negative real part (CT)
Stable for every input matrix B
Decided by the C matrix alone
Stable because the eigenvalue is real
h: CT state stability follows eigenvalue real parts, as with s-plane poles.
f: Step 1: the mode behaves as e^(-506 t). Step 2: it decays, so the model is stable. Check: this is the same left-half-plane rule as Module 5, stated for A.

q: A discrete-time sinusoid cos(pi 461/494 n) has fundamental period N0 =
h: Need Omega0 N / (2 pi) to be an integer, with Omega0 = pi m/k in lowest terms.
f: Step 1: Omega0/(2 pi) = 461/988 after reduction. Step 2: smallest N making Omega0 N a multiple of 2 pi is N = 988. Check: Omega0 x 988 / pi = 922, an even integer multiple relationship holds: True.

q: For x[n] = (0.7186)^n u[n], the value x[4] is:
h: Raise alpha to the power n; u[n] = 1 for n at least 0.
f: Step 1: x[4] = (0.7186)^4. Step 2: value = 0.2667. Check: |alpha| = 0.7186 is below 1, so the sequence decays.

q: A memoryless system is y = x^2 (sample values). Feeding the single sample x = 79 + 168 gives output:
h: Apply the rule to the summed input, do not sum separate outputs.
f: Step 1: summed input = 247. Step 2: y = (247)^2 = 61009. Check: separate outputs would sum to 34465, which differs, proving nonlinearity.

q: For x(t) = u(t) and h(t) = u(t) in a continuous-time LTI system, y(590) is: (spaced-repetition variant 11306)
h: The output is the ramp r(t) = t u(t).
f: Step 1: y(t) = integral from 0 to t of 1 dt = t for t at least 0. Step 2: y(590) = 590. Check: differentiating y returns u(t), the step response relationship h = ds/dt holds.

q: X(s) = 810 / (s (s + 426)). The final value x(infinity) is:
h: Final-value theorem: limit of s X(s) as s tends to 0.
f: Step 1: s X(s) = 810/(s + 426). Step 2: at s = 0 this is 810/426 = 1.9014. Check: the remaining pole at -426 is in the left-half plane, so the theorem applies.

q: y[n] - 0.9122 y[n - 1] = x[n]. The pole of H(z) is at z =
h: Transform: Y(z) (1 - a z^-1) = X(z); the pole solves 1 - a z^-1 = 0.
f: Step 1: H(z) = 1 / (1 - 0.9122 z^-1). Step 2: denominator zero when z = 0.9122. Check: this matches the pair a^n u[n] with a = 0.9122.

q: A sawtooth-type Fourier series has harmonic coefficients b_k = 2A/(k pi). For A = 498 and k = 91, b_k is:
h: Substitute A and k into 2A/(k pi).
f: Step 1: b_k = 2 x 498 / (91 pi). Step 2: = 3.4839 (4 decimal places). Check: coefficients fall as 1/k, slower than a triangle wave (1/k^2) but faster than the constant spectrum of an impulse train.

q: A DFT uses N = 2048 samples taken at fs = 694272 Hz. The bin spacing is: (spaced-repetition variant 11306)
h: Spacing = fs / N.
f: Step 1: spacing = 694272 / 2048. Step 2: = 339 Hz between bins X[k] and X[k+1]. Check: N bins x 339 Hz spans the full 694272 Hz sampling rate.

q: Output power is 93.59 times the input power. The gain in decibels is: (spaced-repetition variant 11306)
h: dB = 10 log10(P2/P1) for powers (20 log10 is for voltages).
f: Step 1: ratio = 93.59. Step 2: 10 log10(93.59) = 19.71 dB. Check: ratio 0.5 gives about -3 dB and ratio 10 gives +10 dB; sign follows gain versus loss.

q: A 64-ary modulation runs at 4035 baud. Its bit rate is:
h: Bit rate = baud x log2(L).
f: Step 1: bits per symbol = log2(64) = 6. Step 2: bit rate = 4035 x 6 = 24210 bps. Check: denser constellations raise rate at fixed baud but need higher SNR for the same error rate.
